headline: A full design-system Tabs is where a dynamic prop closure blocks folding: `styled(TabInternal)` keeps its runtime call, and next-yak's styled lane runs at 0.55× of its own css-prop sibling.

microbench.why: The tab group carries a state matrix, responsive typography and an animated underline through CSS anchor positioning, and the active state arrives as a prop. `next-yak-css` at 159,000 renders/s and `vanilla` at 159,000 tie at the top, both emitting plain elements with one class each. The styled lane cannot follow: `Tab` compiles to `styled(TabInternal)("yWZDb8a7", ({ isActive }) => …)`, and a dynamic interpolation over a custom component leaves the runtime call in place, so `next-yak` lands at 88,200 and only 1.14× above its own `foldStatic: false` lane. Lanes that name classes after their declarations pay in React instead of in the library: `bamboo` books 0.016 ms of lib self-time and still totals 3.10 ms, 2.80 ms of it React writing long class attributes. `emotion` at 22,600 re-hashes the state matrix for every tab.

autocannon.why: `vanilla` at 751 req/s and `next-yak-css` at 671 lead. `next-yak` at 443 and `next-yak-nofold` at 399 finish close together, which is the render story again: with the fold blocked there is little left for it to remove. `panda-props` at 91 req/s is the floor.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

attribution.why: `next-yak-css` at 1.27 ms and `vanilla` at 1.30 ms hold the floor with 0.000 ms of lib self-time. `next-yak` needs 1.92 ms with 0.725 ms of lib time, because the dynamic `isActive` interpolation keeps the runtime `styled()` call alive. Further down the cost leaves the library entirely: `bamboo` spends 2.80 ms of its 3.10 ms inside React, and `panda-props` totals 9.54 ms, the slowest in the case.

hydrate.why: Six lanes hydrate between 44.7 ms and 47.3 ms. `goober` at 186 ms and `styled-components` at 189 ms need four times that, rebuilding a full state matrix in the client before React can attach.

inp.why: Nine lanes answer a tab switch between 7.4 ms and 8.4 ms. `styled-components` needs 11.3 ms, `goober` 15.1 ms, `panda-props` 23.8 ms and `emotion` 26.0 ms, all of them re-deriving the state matrix on the tab that changed.

mount.why: Eight lanes mount between 87.4 ms and 94.8 ms. `goober` at 186 ms, `styled-components` at 192 ms and `emotion` at 213 ms build their sheets during the mount itself.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, and its cost splits in two: 0.872 ms to 0.965 ms for twelve lanes, then 1.63 ms to 1.68 ms for `goober`, `emotion` and `styled-components`, the three that inject their sheet at render time.

payload.why: `vanilla` at 2,690 gz B and `next-yak-css` at 2,707 B set the floor, with `next-yak` adding 805 B for its runtime. The gap to the rest is the widest in the suite: `cnfast` at 22.0 kB and `tailwind-merge` at 21.1 kB carry both a merge runtime and long class lists in the markup, roughly eight times what the leading lanes ship for the same 150 tab groups.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: Scaling the tab count separates static resolution from everything else. `stylex` at 29.1 ms, `vanilla` at 29.1 ms and `next-yak-css` at 30.1 ms hold a line, while `next-yak` reaches 63.7 ms because the blocked fold leaves a runtime call per tab. `panda-props` at 272 ms shows what per-instance object resolution does to a slope.

crossCase: The Example `multifile-composition` shown below is this exact workload with the styled primitives moved into an imported `parts.tsx`, and almost nothing moves: `next-yak` runs 88,200 against 87,000 renders/s, because that module keeps the primitives and their JSX use sites together, which is all folding requires. Contrast the Example `multifile-shop`, where primitives ship for another module's JSX to use and `next-yak` gives up 46% of its throughput.
